rv.q: The National Theatre's production of THE DEEP BLUE SEA is both captivating and atmospheric.
Absorbing though it is to watch, this version of 'The Deep Blue Sea' doesn't take us to those eerie and mysterious depths of love that I think Rattigan's play really had in mind.
McCrory provides a revelatory performance marred only by the occasional slip when first night jitters caused the cast to run over each other's lines a couple of times.
McCrory fills that set with Hester as few can ever have.
